messages:
Alex: Heads up — FinOps dashboard shows a ~28% delta between reserved GPU commitments and actual usage for yesterday. Forecast expected ~420k GPU-mins reserved but billing_export shows ~302k used. Looks concentrated in eu-west-1.
Maya: Oof. Is that across all models or a couple of heavy routes?
Alex: Per-route breakdown points at embedder-v2 batch jobs and rerank routes. Rerank spiked but a bunch of cost lines are tagged as "unknown" so they didn't land in reserved coverage.
finops-bot: ALERT: reserved-coverage-drop detected for eu-west-1 (24h window) — delta 28% — investigating. :rotating_light:
Tom: Could be the kube label rename from last Friday's infra rollout (PR #4823). We changed cost-alloc label from `cost_center` -> `finops_tag` and some jobs didn't pick it up.
Sara: I ran a quick SQL against billing_export to surface top offenders. Quick snippet I used:
```sql
SELECT service, labels, SUM(gpu_minutes) as gpu_min, SUM(cost) as cost
FROM billing_export
WHERE invoice_day = DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
GROUP BY service, labels
ORDER BY gpu_min DESC
LIMIT 10;
```
Sara: Top 3 results: embedder-v2 batch (eu-west-1) — 68k gpu-min, rerank-large (eu-west-1) — 55k gpu-min (many rows labeled NULL), background-rlftasks (us-west1) — 40k gpu-min.
Maya: If labels are NULL we won't apply reserved coverage mapping, so cost falls to on-demand. That explains the burn gap.
Alex: Confirmed — reserved mapping requires `finops_tag` present and matched to reservation pools. Missing tag => no coverage.
InfraOps: Also note: autoscaler in eu-west-1 was bumped to min=6 for a short window during the spike; that increased baseline GPU-mins but shouldn't affect mapping. Logging the event id infra-deploy-2026-03-17-09.
Tom: Actionable steps I see: 1) backfill tags for yesterday's jobs via metadata join (billing_export has instance_id), 2) rerun reserved coverage allocation job, 3) fix kube label rollout to set `finops_tag` on newer deployments.
Maya: + please also run a reconciliation query to show projected savings if we backfill vs if we don't. Need numbers for exec.
Alex: I prepared a quick projection — backfill would move ~18% of yesterday's GPU-mins under reservations, saving ~14k USD/day at current unit rates. Need final verification from billing team.
Sara: I can run the reconciliation. SQL I will use to compute delta:
```sql
WITH candidate AS (
  SELECT invoice_day, project, COALESCE(labels, 'UNLABELED') as tag, SUM(gpu_minutes) gpu_min, SUM(cost) cost
  FROM billing_export
  WHERE invoice_day = DATE_SUB(CURRENT_DATE(), INTERVAL 1 DAY)
  GROUP BY invoice_day, project, tag
)
SELECT *, (gpu_min * reserved_rate_per_min) as hypothetical_reserved_cost FROM candidate;
```
Sara: Will post numbers in ~20m.
finops-bot: NOTE: scheduled-job reserved-allocator failed at 2026-03-17T02:14:03Z — error: "NULL label encountered" — restart recommended.
Tom: That explains why the allocator didn't cover yesterday's late jobs. I will investigate the failure cause (task retry logic).
Maya: Long-term: we should consider automating a fallback that assigns a temporary tag based on project -> reservation mapping when labels are missing, to avoid losing coverage. Also consider weekly reserved commitments for eu-west-1 if utilization stays >85% for 7 days.
Alex: Agree. For immediate steps:
- Alex -> open FINOPS ticket and attach these SQL queries and sample billing lines (FINOPS-211)
- Tom -> root cause of reserved-allocator failure + fix retry (ETA EOD)
- Sara -> run reconciliation numbers and post results (ETA +30m)
- Maya -> run a quick cost-sensitivity calc for adding +10% reserved capacity in eu-west-1 vs current commit (ETA tomorrow)
Tom: I'll also roll back the label change on a canary set to verify tagging behavior.
Sara: Reconciliation snapshot: backfilling tags moves 72k gpu-min into reserved pools, estimated cost delta = -$13,600/day. Detailed CSV attached to FINOPS-211.
Alex: Perfect — thanks. Once FINOPS-211 has artifacts we'll decide whether to backfill and whether to buy an interim weekly commitment.
Maya: Small note — check cloud provider invoice lines for any unaligned credits that might shift numbers. Sometimes marketplace credits cause weirdness in per-route cost.
InfraOps: Logged a separate ticket to verify provider invoice reconciliation (INFRA-998).
Alex: Cool. If no objections I'll mark this thread as actioned and paste FINOPS-211 link when ready. :thumbsup:
Maya: No objections. Thanks team.
Tom: On it.
finops-bot: Thread closed for automated follow-ups; will reopen on FINOPS-211 update.
